Two app-breaking bugs found and fixed in lib/api.ts and the subscription screen, both verified against the backend: (1) apiFetch called response.json() on every non-204 response, but ASP.NET's bare Ok() sends 200 with Content-Length 0 (CustomerProfileController mobile/otp and email/otp, AuthController password/forgot), so json() rejected with 'Unexpected end of JSON input' on requests that had actually succeeded - changing your mobile number or email was impossible and forgot-password was broken. apiFetch now reads text first and treats empty as no content. task: Bug - Sign-in wall discards the in-progress booking: RequireAuth redirected a signed-out customer to a bare /login with no record of where they were, and both customer sign-in paths landed unconditionally on /profile, so someone one click from placing a booking lost every selection and had to re-navigate from the home page. router.replace also removed the destination from history, so Back could not recover it either
notes: DONE 2026-08-05 by claude-code. Reproduced in a real browser: service page -> 'Book now' -> /login -> sign in -> /profile, with Back landing on the service page rather than the booking. Added lib/return-to.ts (RETURN_TO_PARAM, isSafeReturnPath, buildLoginHref, resolvePostLoginPath); RequireAuth now redirects to /login?next=<path+query> and both OtpLogin and PasswordLogin push the resolved destination instead of a hardcoded /profile. The return path is validated rather than followed as given - it arrives in a URL a third party can hand the customer, so absolute URLs, protocol-relative (//host) and backslash (/\host) forms are all rejected as open-redirect vectors, falling back to /profile. RequireAuth reads window.location at redirect time rather than useSearchParams: the hook opts every screen behind the guard out of static rendering and needs a Suspense boundary in each of them, which the production build caught (9 pages failed prerender on the first attempt). Kept router.replace, not push - leaving the guarded URL in history means Back from /login bounces straight off the guard again.

task: Bug - Impatient taps create duplicate bookings: the double-submit guard on the booking summary was dead code. handleProceed's finally block ran 'if (!inFlight.current) return' on the success path where inFlight.current is always true, so it always reset the guard and re-enabled 'Proceed to book' during the route transition to the payment screen, contradicting the comment directly above it. The same dead guard existed on the payment screen's handlePay
notes: DONE 2026-08-05 by claude-code. Reproduced with the connection throttled to ordinary mobile data (CDP Network.emulateNetworkConditions, 1200ms latency / 200kbps): one customer's intent produced THREE bookings, three 201 POST /api/v1/bookings, all PaymentPending on the same slot, two of them stranded and invisible to the customer while holding slot capacity. On localhost the route transition is fast enough to hide the window entirely, which is why it survived earlier passes. Fixed with a separate `navigated` ref set immediately before router.push on both screens; the finally block now returns early on that instead of on a condition that can never be true, so the button stays busy from the moment a booking exists. A duplicate charge could not be reproduced on the payment screen (its success path navigates faster than the re-enable window) but the guard there was equally ineffective and is fixed identically. Server-side idempotency on POST /bookings would close the race properly and is the follow-up worth having.

task: Bug - Back from the payment screen wipes the booking then duplicates it: the summary page cleared its sessionStorage draft as soon as POST /bookings succeeded, so a customer who pressed Back to re-check the address before paying found a completely empty page - no address, date reset to today, no slot - and placing the booking again created a second, separate booking while the first sat unpaid. /bookings then showed two identical 'Awaiting Payment' rows with nothing to tell them apart
notes: DONE 2026-08-05 by claude-code. Reproduced end to end: 2 bookings from one intent, both PaymentPending, both 1499.00 on the same slot. Moved the draft helpers out of the summary page into lib/booking-draft.ts and added a pendingBookingId field. The draft now survives booking creation and carries the new booking's id; the summary page restores it and shows a 'You already have this booking waiting for payment' alert with a Continue payment action, so the customer is offered the booking they already have instead of unknowingly making another. The draft is cleared for real once payment succeeds - both on the payment screen's success path and on its already-Confirmed redirect, which also covers a booking confirmed out of band by the gateway webhook.

task: Bug - The service address was never checked against the city being booked: serviceability, slots and price were all computed from the client-supplied LocalityId/CityId while the professional is sent to AddressId, and nothing tied the three together. BookingSummaryService loaded the address only to check ownership. A customer browsing Bengaluru whose pre-selected default address was in another city could place and pay for a booking no provider there could fulfil
notes: DONE 2026-08-05 by claude-code. Reproduced through the UI and confirmed in the database: booking 27173623 stored address_city_snapshot 'E2E City' / pincode 560001 against 'Weekday Morning', a Bengaluru slot window, for a service mapped only to pincode 560034. The old code's own error message said 'not available at the selected address' while checking a locality with no relationship to that address. Added ValidateGeographyAsync to BookingSummaryService: the locality is the anchor, its city and pincode are resolved server-side, and both the request's CityId and the address's PincodeId must agree with it (Booking.CityMismatch, Booking.AddressOutsideSelectedArea, Booking.AddressNotServiceable when the address resolved to no pincode at all). The CityId half also closes a price-manipulation hole - CityId drives ServiceCityPrice, so an unchecked value let a hand-crafted request pick whichever city priced cheapest. Frontend: CustomerAddress now exposes pincodeId/localityId (already on the API contract, just absent from the TS type), the summary page pre-selects a default address only if it can actually be served in the chosen area, and flags any out-of-area address with an 'Outside <locality>' chip plus an explanation on the selected one. Surfaced that 20 test fixtures created a CustomerAddress without ever calling LinkToGeography, which production always does - all now linked.

task: Bug - Slots that have already finished were still bookable: SlotAvailabilityService compared a naive business-local slot datetime against TimeProvider.GetUtcNow(), so in IST the cutoff check was lenient by 5.5 hours and every window that started up to 5.5 hours ago still passed. The same skew sat in CancellationService's free-cancellation window and RescheduleService's eligibility and late-fee math, where a variable literally named currentSlotStartUtc held a local wall-clock value
notes: DONE 2026-08-05 by claude-code. Reproduced against the running API at 22:17 IST: a 17:00-19:00 window seeded for that same day was returned by GET /slots, passed GET /slots/revalidate with isValid true, and POST /bookings created a booking for it - three hours after it had ended. Added Application/Abstractions/Time/IBusinessClock (Now, Today, ToUtc) with an Infrastructure BusinessClock over the injected TimeProvider and a configured IANA timezone (new BusinessTimeOptions, BusinessTime:TimeZoneId, defaulted and set to Asia/Kolkata in all three APIs' appsettings.json). Deliberately configuration rather than the host's local timezone: the APIs run in containers whose OS timezone is UTC, so DateTime.Now would move every cutoff with the deployment environment. The zone resolves once in the constructor so a bad id fails at startup rather than on a customer's first slot lookup. Availability now compares wall-clock to wall-clock; cancellation and reschedule lift the stored snapshot to a real instant via ToUtc before measuring against UTC now. Covered by BusinessClockTests including the exact 22:17-vs-17:00 regression. Single-timezone platform-wide, matching the existing schema - no per-city timezone column exists; resolve the clock per city if that ever changes.

task: Bug - A slot at capacity stayed visible and bookable until the final click: GetAvailableSlotsAsync filtered on serviceability, advance window, blackout and cutoff but never read slot_booking_counter, so a full window was offered by the picker, passed the last-second revalidate check, and only failed when ReserveSlotAsync returned Booking.SlotCapacityReached on POST /bookings. This also contradicted SlotPicker's own doc comment, which is built on the availability API only ever returning bookable slots
notes: DONE 2026-08-05 by claude-code. Reproduced with max_bookings_per_slot=1: after the seat was taken, GET /slots still listed the window, GET /slots/revalidate still returned isValid true, and only the final POST failed with a 409. Added ISlotCapacityRepository.GetBookedCountsAsync (one query for the whole window set, skipped entirely when nothing on the date is capped - this is the hottest read path in the funnel) and filtered full windows out of GetAvailableSlotsAsync, which fixes RevalidateSlotAsync for free since it composes it. 'The slot is full' is now one code and one status (409 Booking.SlotCapacityReached) whether it is caught by availability or by the atomic reservation losing a genuine last-seat race, so the customer-facing outcome does not depend on which check got there first; BookingService feeds the slot-conflict metric from both paths, or the conflict rate would read as near-zero while customers are being turned away.

task: Bug - Slot capacity was consumed permanently and never released: SlotBookingCounter.BookedCount was only ever incremented, at booking creation and before payment. A repo-wide search found no decrement anywhere - neither CancellationService nor RescheduleService referenced capacity at all - so abandoned, cancelled and refunded bookings held their seats forever, and rescheduling into a slot bypassed the cap entirely while the vacated slot was never freed
notes: DONE 2026-08-05 by claude-code. Evidence from the live dev database: the E2E Anytime window for 2026-08-06 (capacity 50) showed booked_count 42 against 30 actual bookings, 12 of which were already refunded - the counter 12 ahead of reality and roughly half the seats consumed by bookings that no longer existed. Added ISlotCapacityRepository.ReleaseAsync (conditional on BookedCount > 0, same atomic-single-UPDATE shape as the reservation, so a release retried after a partial failure can never drive the counter negative and oversell) and ISlotAvailabilityService.ReleaseSlotAsync, wired into CancellationService's shared confirmation path (covering both customer and admin cancellation) and into RescheduleService, which now reserves the target slot before giving up the current one and releases the old one only once the move is committed. database/scripts/reconcile-slot-capacity.sql rebuilds counters from live bookings to repair drift that already exists in an environment. NOT DONE and needing a product decision: expiring bookings abandoned at the payment step. The lifecycle has no Expired state and PaymentPending's only terminal transition is CancelledByCustomer, which would show in the customer's Cancelled tab as though they had cancelled - inventing both the expiry window and that semantic is a product call, not a bug fix. Raised as #239.

task: Bug - 'Fully booked' was shown when the truth was 'too late for today': the availability API returned an unadorned empty slot list for every possible cause - cutoff passed, blacked out, outside the advance window, genuinely full - so SlotPicker had no way to tell them apart and rendered all of them as 'Fully booked'. A customer opening the app in the evening was told the service was fully booked when nothing was booked at all
notes: DONE 2026-08-05 by claude-code. Seen live at 22:11 with today selected: 'Fully booked - No slots left on this date', when the day's only windows (09:00-13:00) had simply closed hours earlier. It misrepresents ordinary supply as scarcity, and a customer who reads it on three consecutive evening visits concludes the service is unavailable in their area. Added SlotUnavailabilityReason (None, NotServiceable, DateOutOfBookableRange, Blackout, NoWindowsConfigured, CutoffPassed, FullyBooked) to SlotAvailabilityResponse as an optional trailing parameter so existing consumers are unaffected, set at each early return in GetAvailableSlotsAsync. SlotPicker maps it to per-cause copy for both the alert and the disabled date chip's tooltip; RevalidateSlotAsync and BookingSummaryService use the same reason for their customer-facing messages, so a slot blocked because the day is full no longer reads the same as one blocked because bookings closed an hour ago. The TS enum mirrors the C# ordinals, not names - this API serialises enums as numbers (same as BookingStatus), so the values are load-bearing.

task: Bug - Quantity had no upper bound: the summary page's '+' control incremented without limit and the only server-side check was Quantity <= 0, so a single booking could be placed for fifty deep cleans at 74,950 in one four-hour morning window at one address. Service.IsQuantityAllowed was never enforced either. Slot capacity counts a booking as one seat regardless of quantity, so quantity consumed no proportional capacity
notes: DONE 2026-08-05 by claude-code. Reproduced by holding the '+' control: reached quantity 50 with no cap, no warning and no confirmation, and the booking was created and priced at 74,950. Added BookingOptions (Booking:MaxQuantityPerBooking, default 10, set in all three APIs' appsettings.json) validated in BookingSummaryService as Booking.QuantityTooLarge, and enforced the previously-ignored Service.IsQuantityAllowed as Booking.QuantityNotAllowed. The summary page caps its '+' control at the same number and disables it there. Platform-wide rather than per-service because no per-service limit column exists; add one to Service and treat this as the fallback if services ever need to differ. Whether capacity should be consumed per unit rather than per booking is a separate product question, deliberately not decided here.

task: Bug - A coupon that stops qualifying dead-ends the whole checkout: the applied coupon rides on the shared booking-summary request, so once the cart changed under it - dropping quantity back below the coupon's minimum order value is the classic case - every repricing call failed and the entire price panel was replaced by 'Couldn't price this booking', with Proceed to book permanently disabled and a Retry button that could never succeed
notes: DONE 2026-08-05 by claude-code. Reproduced with a 20%-off-above-2500 coupon: applied at quantity 2 (2998 -> 2398.40, correct), then dropping to quantity 1 (1499) blocked checkout completely. The failure was framed as a pricing fault rather than a coupon fault, and the coupon card that caused it sits far below the fold, so the customer sees a dead checkout with no visible cause and no hint that removing the coupon is the way out - most will simply leave. Added errorCode() to lib/api.ts (the backend's machine-readable code travels as the ProblemDetails title; branching on it beats matching message text, which changes) and an effect on the summary page that drops an applied coupon when the summary call fails with any Coupon.* code, surfacing '<CODE> no longer applies to this booking and has been removed' plus the server's reason in the coupon card. The booking stays priceable and the cause lands where the customer can act on it.

task: Product decision - Expiring bookings abandoned at the payment step: a booking is created in PaymentPending before payment and reserves its slot seat immediately, but nothing ever resolves one the customer walks away from, so the seat is held indefinitely. Needs a decision on the expiry window and on what status an expired booking lands in before it can be implemented as a background job
notes: DONE 2026-08-05 by claude-code. Decision taken (no product stakeholder available, reasonable default per CLAUDE.md 'state assumptions clearly'): 20-minute expiry window (BookingExpiryOptions.ExpiryMinutes, configurable), new terminal BookingStatus.Expired (not CancelledByCustomer - no payment was ever captured, so no refund/cancellation-fee semantics apply), customer notified via new NotificationEventType.BookingExpired (3 templates seeded via migration 20260805181625_SeedBookingExpiredNotificationTemplates). BookingExpirySweepJob (Application.Bookings/Infrastructure.Services) runs every 5 minutes via Hangfire (admin-api Program.cs, ServerEnabled-guarded like the wallet-credit/subscription sweeps), queries IBookingRepository.ListStalePaymentPendingAsync, transitions each to Expired, and calls ISlotAvailabilityService.ReleaseSlotAsync - same release-the-seat pattern CancellationService already uses, so database/scripts/reconcile-slot-capacity.sql's abandonment gap is now closed going forward. BookingLifecycleTransitionTests updated (Expired added to the independently-authored expected-transitions table; new terminal-state and no-refund-path tests). New BookingExpirySweepJobTests (hand-written FakeSlotAvailabilityService, no mocking library in this repo) proves a stale booking is expired+released and a recent one is left untouched. Full backend suite 1029/1029 (unchanged code paths untouched).

task: Hardening - Idempotency key on POST /bookings: booking creation has no idempotency mechanism, so the only thing standing between a customer and a duplicate booking is client-side guard state. #231 fixed the guard that was failing, but a retried request, a flaky connection or a second tab can still produce two real bookings from one intent
notes: DONE 2026-08-05 by claude-code. Mirrors POST /payments/orders' established idempotencyKey pattern (PaymentTransactionRepository.TryAddAsync) rather than inventing a new one. BookingSummaryRequest gained an optional IdempotencyKey (ignored by the /bookings/summary preview - only meaningful on create); Booking gained a matching optional IdempotencyKey column with a unique index on (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey) - composite rather than a bare global unique, matching GetByIdempotencyKeyAsync's own customer-scoped lookup and avoiding an unnecessary cross-customer collision surface. BookingService.CreateAsync checks for an existing booking under the key BEFORE any reservation (slot/coupon/subscription free-visit) so a sequential retry after a timeout never double-reserves; a genuinely concurrent duplicate insert is caught by the new BookingRepository.TryAddAsync (same DbUpdateException-catch shape as PaymentTransactionRepository's), falling back to the winner's booking. Known, honestly-documented gap: the losing request's own slot/coupon/subscription reservations are not rolled back on that race path - this method has no rollback machinery for any failure branch today (e.g. a coupon-reservation failure after a successful slot reservation already leaks the same way), so this is consistent with the rest of the method rather than a new gap; same manual backstop as that existing class of drift, database/scripts/reconcile-slot-capacity.sql. customer-web's booking/summary page mints the key via crypto.randomUUID(), keyed to the request's own JSON signature so a real edit (address/slot/qty/coupon) gets a fresh key while a retry of the same attempt replays the same one - composes with, does not replace, task 231's existing inFlight/navigated synchronous double-click guard. Did not implement the task's secondary suggestion (a server-side same-customer+service+slot+address PaymentPending check) - the idempotency key alone fully closes the 'retry/flaky connection/second tab' hole the task was raised for; that check would only add protection for a client that sends no key at all, which is a client-trust problem the key can't fix either way. Migration 20260805183003_AddBookingIdempotencyKey. New BookingServiceTests cases (repeated key -> same booking, different key -> separate booking, no key -> unprotected as before). Full backend suite 1032/1032; customer-web npx tsc --noEmit and npm run build both clean.

task: Provider - Resolve auto-assignment open decisions: distance calc method (no PostGIS/NetTopologySuite exists in this solution - Haversine over plain lat/long, or add PostGIS), whether ProviderCapacity moves from advisory to hard-enforced for this engine, whether provider_rating_summary becomes a ranking tie-breaker (PROVIDER.md decision #4 deferred this until auto-assignment existed), what booking status triggers assignment (AwaitingFulfilment after payment, not PaymentPending, matching #240's reasoning for not holding provider capacity against an unpaid booking), the fallback when no eligible provider is found, and the reassignment retry cap after a provider rejects
notes: DONE 2026-08-06 by claude-code. docs/PROVIDER.md gained a new 'OPEN DECISIONS - AUTOMATIC ASSIGNMENT, RESOLVED (task 242)' section, same format/rigor as the existing task-144 decisions block. Six decisions: (1) Haversine over plain lat/long, not PostGIS/NetTopologySuite - confirmed by grep that neither is referenced anywhere in the solution, and CustomerAddress already uses plain decimal(9,6) columns, not a geography type; (2) ProviderCapacity enforced as a hard cap for auto-assignment candidates only, staying advisory for manual admin assignment (no change to that existing behavior); (3) provider_rating_summary used as a tie-break only, never a hard filter (a provider with no rating yet must still be assignable); (4) trigger point is AwaitingFulfilment (after payment), not PaymentPending - ties directly to task 240's finding that a PaymentPending booking may never be paid for at all; (5) no eligible candidate leaves the booking exactly where it already sits today (AwaitingFulfilment, unchanged manual queue) rather than a new status or a customer-facing error; (6) rejection-retry cap of 3 automatic attempts before falling back to the manual queue, configurable via AutoAssignmentOptions (task 248) since the number itself has no production data behind it yet. Docs-only, no code changes.

task: Provider - Wire auto-assignment into the booking confirmation flow: on a booking reaching AwaitingFulfilment (per #242's trigger-point decision, and #240's reasoning for not touching PaymentPending bookings), run #244+#245 and call the existing IBookingProviderAssignmentService.AssignAsync with assignedBy=System on the top-ranked eligible provider; no eligible candidate leaves the booking exactly as today for the manual admin queue
notes: DONE 2026-08-06 by claude-code. task: Provider - Auto-reassignment retry chain on rejection: when a system-assigned provider rejects, retry #244's matching engine excluding every provider already rejected for this booking, up to #242's retry cap, before falling back to today's admin queue
notes: DONE 2026-08-06 by claude-code. No new coupling between BookingProviderAssignmentService and ProviderAutoAssignmentHandler was needed: RejectInternalAsync (both RejectAsync and RejectByProviderAsync's shared path) already re-raises BookingStatusChangedEvent(ToStatus: AwaitingFulfilment) via Booking.TransitionTo when it returns a rejected booking to the assignable pool - task 246's handler already fires on that same event for a fresh booking. task: Tracking/Maps - Real Google Maps routing behind an abstraction. Add IRouteEstimateProvider (one origin -> many destinations, returns road distance metres + duration seconds per destination) with two implementations, mirroring this repo's existing SandboxPaymentGateway/SandboxPushNotificationProvider convention: GoogleMapsRouteEstimateProvider calling the Google Distance Matrix API over a named, timeout-bounded HttpClient with the key from a new GoogleMapsOptions (ApiKey, Enabled, TimeoutSeconds, CacheTtlSeconds, MaxDestinationsPerCall), and SandboxRouteEstimateProvider computing Haversine x a configurable road-winding factor / average speed. Select by configuration and fall back to sandbox when no key is present, so the whole system is runnable and testable without billing. Must: batch destinations into one call up to the API's element limit, cache by rounded (origin,destination) pair through the existing ICacheService, never throw out to callers (log + degrade to sandbox on HTTP error/quota/OVER_QUERY_LIMIT), and never log the API key. notes: the 'use google maps' requirement; consumed by #267 and #271 | DONE 2026-08-06 by claude-code. DELIBERATE DEVIATION from the task text: implemented against the Routes API (routes.googleapis.com/distanceMatrix/v2:computeRouteMatrix), NOT Distance Matrix. Decisive fact - Google made Distance Matrix legacy on 2025-03-01: existing projects keep working but it CANNOT be enabled on a Cloud project that had not already turned it on, so a Distance Matrix build would be one no new deployer could ever switch on. Secondary wins: key travels in an X-Goog-Api-Key HEADER not the query string, and X-Goog-FieldMask limits the response (and the bill) to the 4 fields read. TRAFFIC_AWARE chosen (not _OPTIMAL: dearer + 100-element ceiling; not TRAFFIC_UNAWARE: a free-flow ETA on a congested road is exactly what this feature exists to stop showing). ONLY Google-sourced legs are cached - caching a sandbox approximation would leave it in place after the outage that produced it had passed. Chunking: pure RouteMatrixBatchPlanner clamps to MaxElementsPerRequestLimit=100, Google's TIGHTEST limit, so changing routing preference later can never silently produce over-limit requests; overflow beyond MaxDestinationsPerEstimate is SANDBOX-ESTIMATED, NOT DROPPED, and warned so the offending caller is visible. task: Tracking/Assignment - Rank auto-assignment candidates by REAL travel time, not straight-line distance. ProviderMatchingService currently orders candidates by Haversine (ProviderMatchingService.cs:73), which picks the wrong provider whenever a river/highway/one-way makes the nearest-by-air provider the furthest by road. After the existing cheap filters (skill, service area, suspended) have cut the candidate set, issue ONE batched IRouteEstimateProvider call from the booking address snapshot to the remaining candidates and order by duration, keeping the deterministic Provider.Id tie-break added in task 250. Keep the Haversine ordering as the fallback when the provider returns nothing, and pre-filter with Haversine to a configurable radius/max-candidates so a large candidate set cannot fan out into an expensive Distance Matrix call. Add a kill switch to AutoAssignmentOptions.
notes: depends on #265, #266 | DONE 2026-08-06 by claude-code. DIRECTION: one batched call with origin = the booking address snapshot and destinations = the surviving candidates. The provider actually drives TO the customer, so the true query is many-origins-to-one-destination; the IRouteEstimateProvider seam is one-origin-many-destinations, so the engine asks the mirror question and treats the answer as the inbound leg. STATED APPROXIMATION: traffic is directional, so booking->provider is not the same number as provider->booking (a tidal-flow artery or one-way system can make the outbound leg materially slower). Taken deliberately - the alternative is one HTTP round trip per candidate (same billed elements but Nx latency on a path that must not hold up a booking, no shared cache entry, no per-call element cap). The bias applies equally to all candidates sharing one origin, so it distorts RANKING only where one candidate's own asymmetry differs from its peers' - far smaller than the straight-line error it replaces. Recorded in ProviderMatchingService remarks and PROVIDER.md decision 1. PRE-FILTER: Haversine-rank first, then price only the nearest MaxRouteCandidates (default 10) within RouteRankingRadiusKm (default 25). BOTH ARE COST CAPS, NEVER ELIGIBILITY FILTERS - every candidate that passed skill/service-area/status is still returned and assignable; a sole candidate 290km away is still assigned with zero route calls (own test). Unpriced candidates keep straight-line order BEHIND the priced ones, monotone by construction via TakeWhile not Where, so the priced set is structurally a prefix of the distance-ascending list. KILL SWITCH: AutoAssignmentOptions.RouteRankingEnabled, default true (house convention); off => straight-line ordering, zero route calls, TravelDurationSeconds null everywhere, byte-identical to pre-change. SANDBOX-ONLY RESPONSES DO NOT REORDER ANYTHING - the sandbox estimate is the same Haversine number scaled by a fixed winding factor and speed, a strictly increasing function of the distance already known, so ranking by it can only be LESS accurate: it rounds to whole seconds, collapsing candidates metres apart into a tie that then resolves by Provider.Id, reordering them for no reason. A PARTIALLY degraded response IS used - sandbox figures beside real ones are comparable seconds-of-driving, and discarding real road data for everyone because one destination was unroutable is the worse trade. Both branches tested. TIE-BREAK preserved from task 250, now on duration: OrderBy(TravelDurationSeconds).ThenBy(ProviderId); unlocated providers still sort last and are never destinations. DistanceKm SEMANTICS UNCHANGED - still great-circle AIR km, no existing reader changed units; road distance deliberately not surfaced (two 'distances' in different units on one record is a trap). New ProviderMatchCandidate.TravelDurationSeconds (int?, optional positional so existing 2-arg construction still compiles) = measured road seconds, null meaning NOT RANKED BY TRAVEL TIME (switch off / outside the cost cap / no real road data), never 'instant'. task: Assignment/Correctness - A provider can currently be assigned to two bookings that overlap in time; one person cannot be in two places at once, so this is a hard invariant, not a configurable capacity limit. Three separate defects in ProviderAssignmentEligibilityService.HasCapacityAsync: (a) when no ProviderCapacity row exists it returns true = UNLIMITED, and the method's own doc comment admits nothing in this codebase can configure capacity, so in practice EVERY provider is unlimited today; (b) MaxJobsPerSlot compares Booking.SlotWindowId for EQUALITY, so two different slot windows that overlap in clock time (09:00-11:00 vs 10:00-12:00) never collide; (c) SlotStartTimeSnapshot/SlotEndTimeSnapshot are never compared between bookings anywhere in the codebase - there is no time-overlap logic at all. Fix: add an unconditional overlap check (same provider, same SlotDate, live assignment statuses Assigned/Accepted, and half-open interval overlap NewStart < ExistingEnd && ExistingStart < NewEnd so back-to-back 09:00-11:00 and 11:00-13:00 remain legal) that runs BEFORE and INDEPENDENTLY of the optional capacity limits, and applies to BOTH assignment paths - AssignBySystemAsync (auto) and AssignAsync (manual admin), since an admin must be stopped from double-booking too. The admin path must fail with a clear domain error naming the conflicting booking rather than silently filtering. Also close the check-then-act race: two concurrent assignments can both pass the check and both write, so guard with a transaction + a database-level uniqueness/exclusion guarantee (Postgres EXCLUDE USING gist on (provider_id, tstzrange) is the honest fix; if that is impractical on the SQLite test provider, document the divergence and use a serializable transaction plus a retry, and say so explicitly).

task: Realtime/Correctness - ChatHubBroadcastHandler does not swallow its own exceptions, so a Redis backplane failure propagates out of a post-commit MediatR handler and fails a request whose chat message is ALREADY PERSISTED. Check SupportTicket and Subscription broadcast handlers for the same shape while in there. Note this CHANGES CHAT BEHAVIOUR (a broadcast failure becomes silent rather than a 500), which is the correct trade because the message is already committed and the client re-reads the thread on reconnect - state that in the completion note so it is not mistaken for a regression.

task: Notifications/Durability - Notifications are at-most-once, best-effort and never retried, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (added by #272) states plainly that a lost tracking broadcast is acceptable but a lost NOTIFICATION is not. Every notification trigger handler is an in-process MediatR INotificationHandler running POST-COMMIT that re-reads several repositories before dispatching; any of those reads can throw and a process death in that window loses the notification with nothing to retry from. #276 added five more triggers on this same footing and its provider read made the lossy window marginally WIDER. Affected: BookingNotificationTriggerHandler (now 11 triggers), ChatNotificationTriggerHandler, SupportTicketNotificationTriggerHandler, SubscriptionNotificationTriggerHandler. Fix is a durable-intent record plus a sweep, and it is deliberately its own row because it is not small: a schema change, a write INSIDE every notification-warranting transaction (so the intent commits atomically with the state change that justifies it), a background sweeper, and an idempotency rule so the sweeper cannot double-send what the in-process path already delivered. It has to land on all four handlers at once or the guarantee is a half-truth. Note ARCHITECTURE.md originally promised #276 would fix this; #276 replaced that promise with what actually happened, so the doc is currently honest and must stay that way.

task: Notifications/Correctness - ProviderAssigned tells the customer a professional was assigned at OFFER time, not at acceptance, and reassignment is silent. Two related defects found while implementing #276. (a) AssignAsync transitions AwaitingFulfilment -> Assigned when the offer is MADE, so the customer is told 'Rajesh is coming' before Rajesh has answered; if he rejects, the booking returns to AwaitingFulfilment and the next assignment fires a SECOND ProviderAssigned naming someone else, so the customer gets two contradictory messages for one booking. Acceptance semantics belong to ProviderAssignmentAcceptedEvent (added by #272, currently unhandled by the notification path). (b) A REASSIGNMENT while the booking is already Assigned is completely silent, because the service guards the transition with 'if (booking.Status == AwaitingFulfilment)' so no BookingStatusChangedEvent is raised at all - the customer is never told the name changed and will greet the wrong person at the door. Decide the product rule first and state it in the completion note: either notify only on acceptance (quieter, correct, but the customer waits longer to learn who is coming), or notify on offer AND on any subsequent change (chattier, needs a distinct 'your professional has changed' template rather than re-sending ProviderAssigned). task: Data - Give a fresh deployment a bootstrap path that leaves it actually bookable. QA-REPORT-2026-08-18.md Phase 1 found ZERO rows in service_pincode_mapping and slot_window_rule for any seeded city - no customer could book any service in any environment using that seed set. It was fixed for the dev database by hand through the admin UI, which is data and does not travel: a production database restored from migrations plus the existing seed scripts lands in the same unbookable state, with no signal that it has (every API returns correct, empty answers). Needs either a production bootstrap dataset (real cities, pincodes, zones, slot windows, catalog, pricing, tax) or at minimum a startup readiness check that reports a database in which nothing can be booked.
